Everyone says time flies when you're having fun. That's not quite it.
Monday's meeting lasts a year. Your weekend lasts ten minutes. Same clock.
Your brain, and it doesn't even own a clock.
Scientists think it guesses the time by counting how often you check.
At your desk, you check constantly, so the seconds pile up.
On a Saturday you're too busy to look, so the counting stops.
Fewer counted seconds, less time. The real clock never slowed.
So time flies when you stop counting. Fun just helps you forget.
Want a longer weekend? Stare at the clock. It works great, and ruins everything.
